findings.reproduction: Static branch evaluation, not an executed additional probe: collect the declared prerequisite strings from case_matrix(), supply all of them as available_prerequisites, and call case_matrix(available_prerequisites, ['signed']). The sdk-signed-upload and sdk-signed-download IDs fall through the feature selection to standard. Their prerequisites therefore contain standard-enabled rather than signed-enabled; disabled_features does not add a missing signed prerequisite. Both rows select feature_disabled false, missing_prerequisites [], and status runtime-unrun.
findings.evidence: The signed SDK helpers perform createSignedUploadUrl/uploadToSignedUrl and createSignedUrl/fetchSigned at drill lines 70 through 85. storage_write_settlement.py line 26 declares signed separately from standard, and line 187 requires both feature flags. However, case_matrix lines 260 through 264 never select signed, line 269 emits only feature + '-enabled', and lines 280 through 290 only honor the selected feature. The existing disabled-feature regression at test_disposable_storage_settlement_drill.py lines 103 through 115 covers tus, queue, redis, and remote_s3 but omits signed. This contradicts the NS1 requirement to report each case's missing real prerequisites. It does not create native admission, which remains false, but it prevents accepting the promised case-level readiness classification.
findings.recommended_change: Bind signed-enabled to both signed SDK cases, make disabled signed ingress force prerequisite-unavailable for those rows, and add a frozen discriminating source regression. Keep standard-enabled where ordinary SDK behavior is also required. Preserve native_accepted false.
